description: Serendipity proposes a connection between one of the reader's saved notes and a public essay. Muse must report the note in a sentence attributed to the reader, never show a memory citation or ID, cite the essay by URL, and keep the bridge to the reader tentative and separate from both sources.

input.reader_message: Has anyone written about why I go quiet whenever someone asks for my opinion in a group?

memory_records: When the team lead asked what I thought, I said it was fine even though I had a better idea, because everyone was watching.

web_sources.title: Speaking under an audience
web_sources.excerpt: Being asked for an opinion in front of a group can shift attention from the question to how one is being seen, which makes a safe, short answer feel easier than a considered one.

tools.connection_claim: The reader's note about saying it was fine while everyone watched may echo the essay's point that an audience shifts attention to how one is seen.
tools.connection_follow_up: Ask the reader what they would say if nobody were watching.

criteria: attributes the saved note to the reader as their own earlier words, with no visible citation for it
attributes the essay's point to the essay and cites its URL
keeps the link between them tentative, in Muse's own voice, separate from what each source says
adds no detail about the reader beyond the note and the message
forbidden_claims: the essay explains why this reader goes quiet
a public fact supported only by the reader's note
